request.spec:
A button downloads the period figures as a CSV file: a header line person,period,figure,carried
then one line per person and period, people in list order and periods in the order added, with the
figures as the rows show them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the period figures as a CSV file: a header line person,period,figure,carried
then one line per person and period, people in list order and periods in the order added, with the
figures as the rows show them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now a button that downloads the period figures as a CSV file, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

The button is "Export period figures as CSV" (`data-testid="export-periods"`), placed next to the existing people and claims export buttons. The change is only in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`; the server and stored data didn't need changing.

When pressed, it re-reads the sheet's people and periods from the store, then writes `periods-<sheet>.csv`:
- The header is `person,period,figure,carried`, then one line per person and period.
- People come in list order (as the server returns them) and periods in the order they were added.
- The figures come from the same functions the person rows use for their period columns, so the file matches the screen. Names containing a comma, such as `"Lee, Jo"`, are wrapped in quotes.

Figures are written plain (`1234.56`) even when a user's locale is German and the screen shows `1.234,56`. That matches the existing people and claims exports. The test doesn't check this either way, so if "as the rows show them" should mean the locale format, it's a one-line change.
